overview.title: Overview
overview.text: Somnath Temple is the first among the twelve Aadi Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva. Located on the western coast of Gujarat, it is a revered pilgrimage site, symbolizing resilience and unwavering faith, having been rebuilt multiple times after destruction.

mythology.title: Mythological Origin
mythology.text: According to legend, the Moon God, Chandra (Soma), was cursed by his father-in-law Daksha to lose his luster. To be relieved of the curse, Chandra worshipped Lord Shiva at this spot. Pleased, Shiva blessed him and took up abode here, becoming known as Somnath, the 'Protector of the Moon God'.

architecture.title: Architectural Highlights
points: Constructed in the Chaulukya style of architecture, also known as the 'Kailash Mahameru Prasad' style.
The temple is situated at a point on the coast where there is no land in a straight line between the shore and Antarctica.
The main spire (Shikhar) is 15 meters high, topped with a pot vessel (Kalash) weighing 10 tonnes.
Built from intricately carved sandstone, depicting various Hindu deities and mythological scenes.
The current temple was reconstructed in 1951 under the guidance of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

significance.title: Spiritual Significance
points: Considered the primary and foremost of the 12 Jyotirlingas.
The site is a 'Triveni Sangam' - the confluence of three holy rivers: Kapila, Hiran, and the mythical Saraswati.
It is believed that a darshan at Somnath cleanses the soul of all sins and ailments.
The temple stands as a powerful symbol of Hindu resurgence and cultural preservation.

events.event: Believed to have been originally built in gold by the Moon God, then in silver by Ravana, and in sandalwood by Krishna.
Destroyed by Mahmud of Ghazni, marking one of several destructions.
A new temple was built nearby by Queen Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore.
The present-day temple was reconstructed and inaugurated by the first President of India, Dr. Rajendra Prasad.

items.text: The sea-facing location is considered highly auspicious and powerful.
A stone pillar, the 'Baan Stambh' (Arrow Pillar), points towards the South Pole, indicating no landmass in between.
The nearby Bhalka Tirth is the place where Lord Krishna is believed to have left his mortal body.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Somnath is not just a temple; it's an emblem of eternal faith, cultural pride, and the indomitable spirit of devotion. A visit here is a journey through history, spirituality, and the serene beauty of the Arabian Sea.

aboutPostCards.title: Major Festivals
items: Maha Shivratri – Celebrated with immense grandeur, attracting lakhs of devotees.
Kartik Purnima Fair – A major fair held for five days in November.
Shravan Maas – The entire month is filled with special pujas and decorations.

aboutPostCards.title: Nearby Attractions
items: Bhalka Tirth – The sacred spot where Lord Krishna was struck by an arrow.
Triveni Sangam Ghat – The confluence point of three holy rivers.
Paanch Pandav Gufa – A temple dedicated to the five Pandava brothers.
Gir National Park – Home to the Asiatic lions, a short drive away.

methods.title: By Road
methods.description: Somnath is well-connected by road to major cities in Gujarat like Ahmedabad, Rajkot, and Porbandar.

methods.title: By Helicopter
methods.description: Helicopter services are generally not available for regular pilgrimage.

methods.title: Nearest Railway
methods.description: Veraval Railway Station is the nearest, located just 7 km away.

methods.title: Nearest Airport
methods.description: Diu Airport (DIU) is about 63 km away, and Rajkot Airport (RAJ) is about 195 km away.
